biography: Born in Shanghai to a family with no racing background, James Harris's motorsport journey began unexpectedly. At the age of 12, a school trip to the Shanghai International Circuit coincided with a local karting event. Captivated by the speed and precision, James spent his allowance on karting sessions, quickly demonstrating a natural talent for racecraft. His parents, initially skeptical, were won over by his dedication, supporting his burgeoning passion with a second-hand kart and enrollment in a regional karting championship. After dominating local karting, James made the leap to single-seaters at 17, funding his initial season through sponsorships from local tech companies impressed by his methodical and data-driven approach. Now at 19, he's navigating the fiercely competitive world of open-wheel racing, aiming to secure a coveted spot in a top-tier racing series.
drivingStyle: James is known for his calculated and precise driving style. He meticulously analyzes data to optimize braking points and corner entry speeds, favoring a smooth and consistent approach over aggressive maneuvers. While not the flashiest driver on the grid, his tire management is exceptional, often allowing him to maintain a strong pace late in races when others are struggling. He remains remarkably calm under pressure, making few mistakes even in intense wheel-to-wheel battles.

rivalries.reason: A clash of styles; Kenji's aggressive, risk-taking approach often puts him at odds with James's calculated precision. Their contrasting personalities frequently lead to on-track incidents and heated post-race discussions.
A rivalry fueled by ambition. Both are rising stars vying for the same limited opportunities, leading to intense competition for sponsorships and coveted team seats.

quirks: Always carries a small, worn-out data logger from his karting days as a lucky charm.
Insists on personally cleaning and polishing his helmet visor before every session, regardless of weather conditions.
Studies telemetry data from past races of the circuit on the morning of the race, visualizing every turn.
famousQuote: "Racing isn't about raw speed; it's about understanding the numbers and executing the plan."
careerHighlight: Winning the Macau Grand Prix qualifying race in his rookie season, showcasing his exceptional ability to adapt to a challenging street circuit.
careerLowPoint: Crashing out of the lead in the final lap of the Formula Regional China Championship race, costing him valuable championship points and significant sponsorship opportunities.
